Tessa — quick legal recommendation based on the facts you shared:

1) Default path: Module 2 (Controller -> Processor) is the appropriate execution route for Galenix as our customer/controller for the primary product use. That maps cleanly to the EU SCCs (Module 2) and we should include the UK Addendum where Galenix has UK-resident data.

Rationale: Galenix will determine the purposes and means of processing for the core inference requests; Redwood acts as processor when serving model inference and storing ephemeral KV/cache logs. Module 2 preserves the controller->processor obligations and liabilities.

2) Processor-to-Processor (Module 3) carve-out: If Galenix expects Redwood to act on a subset of data where Galenix is acting as a processor (rare for them), then Module 3 applies for that narrow flow. In practice we avoid mixed-module complexity by:
  - Keeping logging/analytics under contractual processor obligations (Redwood as processor) and
  - Documenting any downstream subprocessors in Annex I and applying standard subprocesser clauses.

3) UK Addendum: Yes — include the UK Addendum for transfers of personal data originating from the UK. We should prepare the EU SCCs execution package + UK Addendum template.

4) Next steps & timing: I will attach Redwood's preferred Module 2 SCCs template and a redlined DPA draft. Recommend sending: Redwood_DPA_for-signing.pdf and Redwood_SCCs_Module2_Template.docx via DocuSign. We can hit a two-week signature target provided Galenix's legal returns comments within 4 business days.

Attachments: Redwood_SCCs_Module2_Template.docx, Redwood_DPA_for-signing.pdf
